notes: The session's web search allowance ran out after the five searches for the legislative candidates. Everything else was read at known addresses with the kit's honest User-Agent (states/net.py), each page checked against its site's robots.txt first: governments' own sites, the Legislative Reference Library, one local party unit, and the campaign websites already filed with the Secretary of State. No search engine was read in place of the search tool.

Not reached, so no findings: the City of Hugo's site asks scripts to stay out (robots.txt), so Tom Weidt is blank; Houston County's site failed the TLS handshake (Eric Johnson); the City of Grand Rapids' site closed the connection (Dale Adams); Perham-Dent's district site timed out (Duane (DJ) Altstadt Jr); Dakota County's commissioner pages are drawn by script and showed no names (Laurie Halverson's facts are from the Legislative Reference Library); the Minnesota Judicial Branch site was not asked, since it answered earlier parts with 403 (Gina M Brandt, Tricia Loehr).

Looked for on their body's own page and not listed as sitting members, so blank: Rachel Lucas (North St. Paul council), Donna Tarantino-Walker (Victoria council), Marcy Kim Busho (Owatonna council), Kurt Christianson (Detroit Lakes board), Michael A. Rivera Jr. (Farmington board), Dan Wolf (Grand Rapids ISD 318 board), Debra Dodge (Buffalo-Hanover-Montrose board).

Stacey Stout's birth year and her 2012 and 2014 runs come from the University of Minnesota Libraries' Minnesota Historical Election Archive, labelled secondary; it is an academic compilation, not Wikipedia or a news organization, so the verifier or John may prefer to drop it. The archive's page ties her to Mahtomedi and the Mahtomedi School Board, as her campaign site does.

No party's own page naming an endorsement was found for Chris Knoll, Zach Duckworth, Stacey Stout or Bianca Virnig (the state Republican nominees page lists statewide offices only; local unit addresses were not known without search). Knoll's own site says he is the endorsed Republican candidate, kept as own_words.

Privacy: one early read of a campaign home page printed the committee's street address and phone line from the page footer to the working log; nothing of it was stored, and the reader was changed to mask phone numbers, e-mail and street addresses before any further page was read.

Verifier, 2026-10-02: every address was re-opened with the kit's User-Agent and each fact read on the page. Corrected: Laurie Halverson's commissioner entry now ends as the Library writes it (2021 to ?), not now; Chad Johnson's source no longer cites a second page that has no address in this file. For John: Stacey Stout's 2012 and 2014 runs rest on a university archive labelled secondary; drop them if only Wikipedia and news organizations may be secondary.
